newsitem.title: UK: Salt water encroaching on Nile Delta, scientists say.
newsitem.headline: Salt water encroaching on Nile Delta, scientists say.

text.p: The Nile Delta is slowly sinking into the sea, geologists warned on Wednesday.

The slow subsidence does not mean immediate floods but could mean precious farmland may become soaked in salt, rendering it useless, Daniel Smith and colleagues at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington said.
Combined with a gradual rise in sea level, the whole area is losing about five mm (two tenths of an inch) a year, they wrote in a report in the science journal Nature.
"If you are being extremely conservative, with a rise in sea level of five mm, in one century you're at 50 cm. That is a lot," Stanley said in a telephone interview.
He said parts of the region were already below sea level and the heavily populated Delta cities of Port Fuad and Port Said risked losing farmland. "
"If nothing were done the extent of shoreline could encroach into the land by as much as 20 to 30 km by the end of the next century," Smith said.
